VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The proof constructs a nondegenerate subinterval \([p,q]\) around a point where \(f>0\) using \(\max\) and \(\min\) to stay within \([a,b]\); step 3.1 proves \(p<q\) even when \(c\) is an endpoint, and the oriented integral convention correctly assigns \(0\) to any degenerate outer pieces. Every edge case (\(c=a\), \(c=b\), \(\delta\) large, etc.) is addressed and the reasoning holds.
SOURCES: All twelve declared dependencies and their cited facts were inspected. The key results—thm-continuous-implies-integrable, lem-integrability-on-a-subinterval, thm-additivity-over-subintervals (claim 3), thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral (claims 1 and 3), lem-integral-elementary-bounds, def-continuity-real, and def-oriented-integral—are used exactly as their statements allow, without mismatched hypotheses or conclusions.
CHECKED: Title, public claim, every numbered step (1.1 through 6.1), and the Remarks were reviewed; no fatal error, missing necessary hypothesis, or invalid inference was found.
